purpose: Test whether the main anthropogenic host-resource expansion and host-contribution concentration results depend materially on crop host taxa.

crop_reference.authority: FAO Indicative Crop Classification (ICC), Appendix 4 botanical crop list
crop_reference.source_scope: Alphabetical list of crops with botanical names and ICC codes
crop_reference.rationale: External agricultural classification fixed independently of butterfly results.

strict.rule: Exclude host taxa whose HOSTS input name or WCVP accepted name matches an explicit species-level botanical name in the FAO ICC list after binomial normalization.
strict.note: Infraspecific crop names are normalized to their parent binomial.

conservative.rule: Apply the strict exclusion and additionally exclude any host whose genus is represented by a genus-level FAO crop entry such as 'Avena spp.' or 'Rubus spp.'.
conservative.note: This deliberately over-excludes possible wild congeners and is interpreted as an upper-bound crop sensitivity.

invariants.introduced_status_interpretation: WCVP introduced wild distribution only; cultivated-only or merely planted non-self-reproducing records are not included.

outputs: aggregate native and contemporary species-by-WGSRPD3 units and percent increase
number and fraction of butterflies with positive added opportunity
Spearman host-family breadth versus log resource expansion
host contribution concentration: hosts needed to account for 50% of fractional added opportunity
median effective contributor number and maximum single-host fractional share in the original adequate subset after crop exclusion

interpretation.manuscript_policy: Report in SI; main text receives at most one sentence that conclusions were unchanged if both sensitivity tiers preserve the qualitative conclusions.
